summary: Record person availability: status override, interruptions, deadline clock and raw device states, each with its daemon-assigned source; asks may carry a priority

replay.detail: Four new durable or current claim kinds on person/NAME replay through the generic claim log. Reads fold them at read time; no projection table is added, so replay rebuilds nothing new.

schema.detail: Adds person.status-set (status available|away|null), person.interruptions-set (all|urgent|none) and person.deadline-clock-set (run|hold-routine|hold-all), each with optional until_unix_ms and a required daemon-assigned source, and person.presence-observed (state active|inactive|locked|sleeping, optional last_input_at_unix_ms, observed_at_unix_ms, source). person.directive-note-set gains optional source, and work.person-asked gains optional priority (critical|high|normal|low). The claim-registry digest changes and the convergence corpus moves to claims-v26.json.

rules.detail: Only the subject person may write these kinds, on every admission path including replication; the ordinary claim surface refuses them. Devices report raw state only; the daemon derives presence for every device alike: active is present until 10 minutes after its last input, then idle; inactive is idle; locked and sleeping are locked. A device's newest state counts for 24 hours. Without an override, status is available while some device is present, away while devices count but none is present, and available with source unreported when none counts. A report is recorded only when it changes the device's state or derived presence, or moves an active device's last input forward by 5 minutes; a report observed before the device's newest recorded report is never recorded, so a delayed report cannot replace a newer state. An ask is urgent exactly when its priority is critical. Availability informs and never grants authority.

compatibility.detail: Adding the claim kinds and the optional fields changes the claim-registry digest; existing mismatched-registry guards apply until every member runs a build that recognizes them. Older members retain the new claims as retryable unknown-kind records, and the new optional fields as unknown fields, and replay them after upgrading.

downtime.detail: No startup migration or service interruption.

manual.detail: No operator action. Nothing writes these claims until the client operations that follow are deployed.

recovery.detail: The claims are authoritative and append-only; a person corrects availability by writing a newer value.
